::: {.piege}
```{r}
folder <- tempfile()
dir.create(folder)
files <- c("data.csv", "data.csv.bak", "notes_csv.txt", "xcsv.R")
created <- file.create(file.path(folder, files))
list.files(folder, pattern = "*.csv")
```
:::

## Why

The `pattern` argument of `list.files()` is a regular expression, as in `grepl()`, and not a shell wildcard. In a regular expression, `.` means any character and `*` repeats what comes before it: a leading `*` has nothing to repeat and is ignored. `*.csv` therefore means "any character followed by csv, anywhere in the name": `_csv` and `xcsv` fit, and nothing ties the pattern to the end of the name.

The line looks right, and it works as long as the folder only holds the expected files. The day a backup or a notes file lands there, the script reads it too.

## The remedy

Escape the dot and anchor the end of the name: `"\\.csv$"`. To keep the wildcard syntax, translate it with `glob2rx()`.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
list.files(folder, pattern = "\\.csv$")
glob2rx("*.csv")
list.files(folder, pattern = glob2rx("*.csv"))
```
:::
